docs.title: DXL2-C — DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 in C
docs.text: Quick start

docs.title: A minimal device in one file
docs.text:
Two callbacks connect the library to your hardware: a write function for the UART and a handler for received packets. This device answers PING with its model number and firmware version.

#include "dxl2.h"

static struct dxl2_link link;

static int uart_write(void* context, const uint8_t* data, size_t length)
{
    (void) context;
    return board_uart_write(data, length); /* 0 on success */
}

static void on_packet(const struct dxl2_packet* packet, void* context)
{
    static const uint8_t ping_reply[] = {0x06, 0x04, 0x26}; /* model 1030, firmware 38 */

    (void) context;
    if ((packet->id == 1U) && (packet->instruction == DXL2_INST_PING))
    {
        (void) dxl2_link_send_status(&link, 1U, DXL2_ERR_NONE, ping_reply, sizeof(ping_reply));
    }
}

int main(void)
{
    const struct dxl2_link_config config = {.write = uart_write, .handler = on_packet};

    (void) dxl2_link_init(&link, &config);
    for (;;)
    {
        uint8_t bytes[32];
        const size_t count = board_uart_read(bytes, sizeof(bytes));

        dxl2_link_receive(&link, bytes, count);
    }
}

board_uart_write() and board_uart_read() stand for your board's UART driver. The examples are complete programs for bare metal, Zephyr and a PC serial port.

docs.title: Little-endian helpers
docs.text:
static inline uint16_t dxl2_get_u16(const uint8_t* data);
static inline uint32_t dxl2_get_u32(const uint8_t* data);
static inline void dxl2_put_u16(uint8_t* data, uint16_t value);
static inline void dxl2_put_u32(uint8_t* data, uint32_t value);

Read or write a 16- or 32-bit value in little-endian byte order, independent of the CPU's byte order and alignment. data must point to 2 (or 4) accessible bytes; the helpers do not check it, like memcpy().

docs.title: Limits and errors
docs.text: Macro Value Meaning DXL2_MAX_PARAMETER_SIZE DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE - 10U Largest unstuffed parameter block (246 by default) DXL2_PARSE_ERROR -1 Invalid argument, malformed packet, CRC mismatch or insufficient capacity

docs.title: struct dxl2_packet
docs.text:
One decoded packet, with byte stuffing removed.

struct dxl2_packet
{
    uint8_t id;                                  /* source or destination ID */
    uint8_t instruction;                         /* instruction, 0x55 for Status */
    uint16_t parameter_length;                   /* number of valid bytes in parameters */
    uint8_t parameters[DXL2_MAX_PARAMETER_SIZE]; /* unstuffed parameters */
};

For a Status Packet, parameters[0] is the error byte and the data follows from parameters[1].

docs.title: struct dxl2_parser
docs.text:
State of the incremental parser for one byte stream. Treat the members as private. Initialize it with dxl2_parser_init() before use.

struct dxl2_parser
{
    uint8_t buffer[DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE]; /* packet in progress, header to CRC */
    size_t length;                        /* number of bytes in buffer */
};

docs.title: dxl2_crc16()
docs.text:
uint16_t dxl2_crc16(const uint8_t* data, size_t length);

Computes the Protocol 2.0 CRC-16: polynomial 0x8005, initial value 0, not reflected, no final XOR.

Parameter Description data Bytes covered by the CRC length Number of bytes

Returns the CRC, or 0 (the initial value) when data is NULL.

docs.title: dxl2_parser_init()
docs.text:
void dxl2_parser_init(struct dxl2_parser* parser);

Resets a parser before a new byte stream, or to discard a partial packet. NULL is ignored.

docs.title: dxl2_parser_feed()
docs.text:
int dxl2_parser_feed(struct dxl2_parser* parser, uint8_t byte, struct dxl2_packet* packet);

Feeds one byte to the parser. The parser searches for the header, checks the Length field, waits for the complete packet, validates the CRC and removes byte stuffing. Keep feeding bytes after an error: the parser resynchronizes on the next header.

Parameter Description parser Initialized parser state byte Next byte of the stream packet Output packet; its contents are valid only when the call returns 1 Return Meaning 1 A complete, valid packet is in packet 0 More bytes are needed DXL2_PARSE_ERROR NULL argument, invalid Length, CRC mismatch or invalid byte stuffing; the parser has been reset

docs.title: dxl2_encode()
docs.text:
int dxl2_encode(uint8_t id, uint8_t instruction, const uint8_t* parameters,
                uint16_t parameter_length, uint8_t* output, size_t output_capacity,
                size_t* output_length);

Encodes a complete wire packet: header, ID, Length, instruction, parameters with byte stuffing, and CRC.

Parameter Description id Packet ID instruction Instruction byte parameters Unstuffed parameters; may be NULL when parameter_length is 0 parameter_length Number of parameter bytes, at most DXL2_MAX_PARAMETER_SIZE output Buffer that receives the packet output_capacity Size of output; at least 10 output_length Receives the packet length on success Return Meaning 0 Packet encoded; *output_length bytes of output are valid DXL2_PARSE_ERROR NULL argument, too many parameters, or the stuffed packet does not fit in output_capacity

A buffer of DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE bytes holds every packet the link can send. The encoder never writes beyond output_capacity.

docs.title: dxl2_write_fn
docs.text:
typedef int (*dxl2_write_fn)(void* context, const uint8_t* data, size_t length);

Writes one complete wire packet to the transport. Called by dxl2_link_send() and dxl2_link_send_status().

Parameter Description context write_context from the link configuration data The encoded packet; valid only during the call length Number of bytes

Returns 0 on success or a negative value on failure; the value is passed back to the caller of the send function.

docs.title: dxl2_packet_handler_t
docs.text:
typedef void (*dxl2_packet_handler_t)(const struct dxl2_packet* packet, void* context);

Called by dxl2_link_receive() for every valid packet. packet is valid only until the handler returns; copy what you need. The handler may send on the same link.

Parameter Description packet The decoded packet context handler_context from the link configuration

docs.title: struct dxl2_link_config
docs.text:
struct dxl2_link_config
{
    dxl2_write_fn write;           /* NULL makes the link receive-only */
    void* write_context;           /* passed to write */
    dxl2_packet_handler_t handler; /* NULL discards packets (they are still counted) */
    void* handler_context;         /* passed to handler */
};

docs.title: struct dxl2_link
docs.text: The state of one link: a copy of the configuration, a parser, the last packet and two counters. Allocate it yourself and treat its members as private.

docs.title: dxl2_link_init()
docs.text:
int dxl2_link_init(struct dxl2_link* link, const struct dxl2_link_config* config);

Initializes a link: copies the configuration, resets the parser and the counters.

Return Meaning 0 Link ready DXL2_PARSE_ERROR link or config is NULL

docs.title: dxl2_link_receive()
docs.text:
void dxl2_link_receive(struct dxl2_link* link, const uint8_t* data, size_t length);

Feeds received bytes, in any chunking, to the link's parser. For each valid packet it increments the receive counter and calls the handler; each rejected packet increments the invalid-packet counter. Does nothing if link or data is NULL.

Call it for a given link from one context only, and not from an interrupt handler.

docs.title: dxl2_link_send()
docs.text:
int dxl2_link_send(struct dxl2_link* link, uint8_t id, uint8_t instruction,
                   const uint8_t* parameters, uint16_t parameter_length);

Encodes a packet into a stack buffer of DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE bytes and passes it to the write function.

Return Meaning 0 Packet written DXL2_PARSE_ERROR NULL link, no write function, invalid parameters, or the packet does not fit other negative value Returned by the write function

docs.title: dxl2_link_send_status()
docs.text:
int dxl2_link_send_status(struct dxl2_link* link, uint8_t id, uint8_t error,
                          const uint8_t* data, uint16_t data_length);

Sends a Status Packet with instruction 0x55: the error byte followed by data.

Parameter Description id ID of the answering device error DXL2_ERR_*, optionally ORed with DXL2_ERR_ALERT_BIT data Status data; may be NULL when data_length is 0 data_length Number of data bytes, at most DXL2_MAX_PARAMETER_SIZE - 1

Returns the same values as dxl2_link_send(). Invalid data or data_length returns DXL2_PARSE_ERROR before anything is written.

docs.title: dxl2_link_rx_packets(), dxl2_link_invalid_packets()
docs.text:
uint32_t dxl2_link_rx_packets(const struct dxl2_link* link);
uint32_t dxl2_link_invalid_packets(const struct dxl2_link* link);

Return the number of valid and of rejected packets since dxl2_link_init(), or 0 for a NULL link. The counters wrap around at 2^32.

docs.title: Return codes summary
docs.text: Value Meaning 0 Success (dxl2_parser_feed(): need more bytes) 1 dxl2_parser_feed() only: a complete valid packet is available DXL2_PARSE_ERROR (-1) Invalid argument, malformed packet, CRC mismatch, or insufficient capacity other negative dxl2_link_send*() only: value returned by the write function

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: This chapter explains the internal structure of DXL2-C: its layers, how a byte becomes a packet and a packet becomes bytes, how the parser recovers from errors, and the rules for memory, errors and concurrency that follow from the design.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
The library has three layers. Each one depends only on the layers below it.

Layer Header Responsibility Definitions dxl2_defs.h Instruction and error values from the specification, broadcast ID, little-endian helpers. No state, no functions with side effects. Codec dxl2_protocol.h CRC-16, the incremental stream parser and the encoder. Pure functions over caller-owned buffers. Link dxl2_link.h Glue between the codec and a transport: owns a parser, dispatches packets to a handler, sends packets through a write function, counts good and bad packets.

dxl2.h includes all of them, together with the build-time configuration in dxl2_config.h. Applications normally include only dxl2.h.

You can use the codec without the link — for example in a tool that parses a log file, or in firmware that already has its own message dispatcher. The link is a thin convenience layer (about 100 lines) on top of the codec.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
Receive path. Your transport delivers bytes — typically a UART interrupt puts them in a queue, and a main loop or thread takes them out. You pass them to dxl2_link_receive() in chunks of any size. The link feeds them one at a time to dxl2_parser_feed(). Whenever the parser completes a valid packet, the link increments its rx_packets counter and calls your packet handler with a pointer to the decoded packet. Rejected packets increment invalid_packets and are otherwise ignored.

Transmit path. To send, you call dxl2_link_send() (any instruction) or dxl2_link_send_status() (a Status Packet). The link encodes the packet into a buffer on its own stack with dxl2_encode(), which adds the header, Length, byte stuffing and CRC, and then passes the complete packet to your write function in one call.

The handler runs inside dxl2_link_receive(), in the context that called it. It may send replies on the same link directly: transmitting does not touch the parser.

docs.title: The parser
docs.text:
dxl2_parser_feed() consumes exactly one byte per call and returns 1 (packet ready), 0 (need more bytes) or DXL2_PARSE_ERROR. Internally it keeps the bytes of the packet in progress in struct dxl2_parser:

  1. Append. The new byte is stored at the end of the buffer.
  2. Synchronize. While the buffer holds at least four bytes that are not the header FF FF FD 00, the first byte is dropped. This sliding window discards noise and partial packets and lines the buffer up with the next header.
  3. Check the Length. Once seven bytes are present (header, ID, Length), the Length field is checked: it must be at least 3 (instruction and CRC) and the whole packet must fit in DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE. A bad Length is rejected at once, without waiting for bytes that may never come.
  4. Wait. Until 7 + Length bytes are present, the parser returns 0.
  5. Validate and decode. The CRC is checked over the stuffed bytes, exactly as they were sent. Then byte stuffing is removed while the instruction and parameters are copied into struct dxl2_packet. A header sequence without its stuffing byte is a malformed packet.
  6. Reset. After a packet — valid or not — the parser buffer is emptied and the next byte starts a new search.

The cost per byte is constant except for the synchronization step, which moves at most DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE bytes. There is no recursion and no data-dependent loop without a fixed bound, so the worst-case execution time is easy to bound.

Recovery after errors

The bytes of a rejected packet are discarded. If a lost byte makes the Length field reach into the next packet, that packet is rejected too, and the parser locks onto the one after it. Controllers should treat a missing reply as a timeout and retry.

docs.title: The encoder
docs.text:
dxl2_encode() writes the header and ID, then copies the instruction and parameters into the output buffer. After every byte it checks whether the last three bytes written are FF FF FD; if so, it inserts an extra FD. It then fills in the Length field — which counts the stuffed bytes — and appends the CRC computed over everything before it.

The output capacity is checked before every byte is written, so an undersized buffer returns DXL2_PARSE_ERROR instead of overflowing. The worst case for stuffing is one extra byte per three parameter bytes; with DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE as the capacity, every packet that the parser accepts can also be encoded.

docs.title: Memory model
docs.text:
All state lives in two structures that you allocate — statically, on a stack or inside your own objects:

Structure Contents Size with the default configuration struct dxl2_parser bytes of the packet in progress, their count 256 bytes + size_t struct dxl2_packet ID, instruction, parameter count, unstuffed parameters 250 bytes struct dxl2_link configuration, one parser, the last packet, two counters ≈ 550 bytes on a 32-bit MCU

The library has no global variables except one read-only table (the header bytes), never calls malloc(), and allocates only fixed-size buffers on the stack: one packet buffer in dxl2_link_send() and one parameter buffer in dxl2_link_send_status(). The measured stack usage per function is listed in Configuration.

Because nothing is shared, you can have as many links as you have buses, each with its own configuration.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Every function reports errors through its return value; nothing is printed, logged or asserted.

Situation Result A NULL pointer or inconsistent length passed to a function DXL2_PARSE_ERROR (or 0 for dxl2_crc16() and the counters); nothing is written A packet with a bad Length, CRC or byte stuffing dxl2_parser_feed() returns DXL2_PARSE_ERROR; the link counts it in invalid_packets A packet that does not fit in the output buffer dxl2_encode() and dxl2_link_send*() return DXL2_PARSE_ERROR The write function fails dxl2_link_send*() return the write function's own (negative) value A corrupted parser structure (for example, never initialized) dxl2_parser_feed() resets it and returns DXL2_PARSE_ERROR instead of writing out of bounds

Protocol-level errors that a device reports — an unknown instruction, an address out of range — are not library errors. Your handler sends them back as the error byte of a Status Packet (DXL2_ERR_*).

docs.title: Threading and reentrancy
docs.text:
The library contains no locks, by design: the right primitive depends on your system, and a hidden mutex would make the library unusable in interrupt-only firmware.

  • Codec functions are reentrant. They only touch the buffers you pass in, so they can be called from any context, concurrently, as long as each call has its own buffers.
  • A link is not thread-safe. Call dxl2_link_receive() for a given link from one context only. Do not call it from an interrupt handler: the packet handler runs inside it and usually transmits.
  • Sending from several contexts at once (for example an RX thread replying and an application thread sending commands) needs a mutex around your write function, or around the dxl2_link_send*() calls.
  • The packet handler receives a pointer into the link. The data is valid only until the handler returns; copy what you need to keep.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text: Decision Reason One byte per parser call Works with any transport chunking, including single-byte interrupts, with no internal buffering policy to configure. CRC checked before unstuffing The CRC is defined over the bytes on the wire; checking first rejects corrupted packets before any data is copied. Fixed-size buffers from one macro Memory use is known at build time and can be reviewed; one macro scales everything consistently. Callbacks for I/O The library never needs to know about drivers or operating systems, and it is trivial to test with mocks. int status codes Lets an existing driver write() function be used as the write callback without a wrapper; recorded as MISRA deviation DEV-01.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to DXL2-C are listed here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project uses Semantic Versioning: the public API in dxl2.h and inc/ stays compatible within a major version.

docs.text:

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Build-time parameters live in inc/dxl2_config.h. Each one is guarded by #ifndef, so override it with a compiler definition instead of editing the file:

target_compile_definitions(dxl2 PUBLIC DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE=1024U)
Parameter Default Meaning DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE 256U Largest complete wire packet (header to CRC) the parser and encoder accept; 10U..65542U, checked at compile time

Derived values:

Macro Value DXL2_MAX_PARAMETER_SIZE DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE - 10U

docs.title: Memory footprint
docs.text:
DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE sizes three buffers:

Object Size struct dxl2_parser DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE + size_t struct dxl2_packet DXL2_MAX_PARAMETER_SIZE + 4 bytes struct dxl2_link parser + packet + configuration + two counters dxl2_link_send() stack DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE dxl2_link_send_status() stack DXL2_MAX_PARAMETER_SIZE + the dxl2_link_send() frame

docs.title: Stack usage
docs.text:
The library does not recurse and does not use variable-length arrays, so the stack depth is fixed. Measured with -fstack-usage, default DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE (256), bytes per function frame:

Function Cortex-M4 -Os Cortex-M4 -O0 x86-64 -O2 dxl2_link_send_status() 272 296 336 dxl2_link_send() 296 312 368 dxl2_encode() 24 56 32 dxl2_crc16() 8 32 8 dxl2_link_receive() 24 32 80 dxl2_parser_feed() (with dxl2_decode_packet()) 32 32 + 56 80 dxl2_link_init() 16 32 48 other functions 0 16 8

Toolchains: Arm GNU Toolchain 15.2 (-mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb), GCC 14.2. At -O0 the small static functions (dxl2_get_u16(), dxl2_parser_reset()) add 16 bytes each where they are called.

Worst-case call chains on Cortex-M4 -Os, without the callbacks:

Path Chain Stack Transmit dxl2_link_send_status → dxl2_link_send → dxl2_encode → dxl2_crc16 600 B + write callback Receive dxl2_link_receive → dxl2_parser_feed → dxl2_crc16 64 B + packet handler Receive and reply dxl2_link_receive → handler → transmit chain 624 B + handler + write

The two large frames are the transmit buffers, so they scale with DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE: about 2 × DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE + 90 bytes for the transmit chain. Measure your own build with:

arm-none-eabi-gcc -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -Os -std=c11 -fstack-usage -Iinc -I. -c src/dxl2_link.c src/dxl2_protocol.c
cat *.su

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The repository contains three complete example programs in examples/. They show the integration patterns from the integration guide in working code.

Example Role Platform Built and run in CI Bare metal Device Any MCU; runs on a PC against a simulated board Yes, as a self-checking test Host serial port Controller Linux, macOS, Windows Built Zephyr Device Any Zephyr board with a UART No, needs a Zephyr workspace

Build the host examples and run the bare-metal test:

ctest --test-dir "build/DXL2[Examples]" -L example --output-on-failure

docs.title: Bare metal
docs.text:
examples/bare_metal is a DYNAMIXEL device for a microcontroller without an operating system. It answers PING, READ and WRITE on a 128-byte Control Table whose first 64 bytes are read-only.

File Contents main.c The application: ring buffer, main loop, packet handler, Control Table board.h The four board functions the application needs board_host.c A PC implementation of board.h that turns the example into a test

Structure. The UART interrupt calls app_uart_rx_isr() for every byte. It stores the byte in a single-producer, single-consumer ring buffer and returns. The main loop takes bytes out of the buffer and passes them to dxl2_link_receive(); when the buffer is empty it calls board_idle(), which on a real MCU executes WFI until the next interrupt. The packet handler therefore runs in the main loop, never in the interrupt.

for (;;)
{
    if (rx_tail != rx_head)
    {
        const uint8_t byte = rx_queue[rx_tail];

        rx_tail = (uint16_t) ((rx_tail + 1U) & (RX_QUEUE_SIZE - 1U));
        dxl2_link_receive(&link, &byte, 1U);
    }
    else
    {
        board_idle();
    }
}

The ring buffer needs no lock on a single-core 32-bit MCU: the interrupt writes only rx_head, the main loop writes only rx_tail, and 16-bit loads and stores are atomic. On an 8-bit MCU, disable the RX interrupt around the comparison.

Porting. Implement board.h for your MCU:

Function What it must do board_init(baud_rate) Configure the UART (8N1) and enable its RX interrupt; call app_uart_rx_isr() from it board_uart_write(data, length) Transmit the bytes and wait until the last one has left the shift register, then switch a half-duplex transceiver back to receive board_idle() Sleep until the next interrupt (__WFI() on Cortex-M)

The simulated board. board_host.c acts as the controller. Each time the main loop goes idle, it checks the reply to the previous request and injects the next one — preceded by line noise, so the parser must resynchronize. The test covers PING (direct and broadcast), a PING for another ID, READ, WRITE, a broadcast WRITE without a reply, a write to a read-only address, out-of-range and malformed READs, and an unsupported instruction:

bare-metal example on the host simulator, 57600 bit/s
PING                         ok
broadcast PING               ok
PING to another ID           ok
READ model number            ok
WRITE RAM                    ok
READ RAM                     ok
broadcast WRITE              ok
READ after broadcast WRITE   ok
WRITE read-only ID           ok
READ out of range            ok
READ with bad length         ok
unsupported instruction      ok
0 failure(s)

docs.title: Host serial port
docs.text:
examples/host_serial builds dxl2_ping, a command-line controller that sends a PING through a serial port and lists every device that answers.

dxl2_ping /dev/ttyUSB0            # broadcast PING at 57600 bit/s
dxl2_ping COM3 1000000 1          # PING ID 1 at 1 Mbit/s

Example output with two XL430-W250 servos on the bus:

ID   1: model 1060, firmware 52
ID   2: model 1060, firmware 52
2 device(s) answered, 0 invalid packet(s)
File Contents main.c Argument parsing, the link, the Status Packet handler serial_port.h Four functions: open, write, read with timeout, close serial_port_posix.c Linux and macOS implementation with termios and poll() serial_port_win32.c Windows implementation with the Win32 communications API

After sending, the program reads with a 50 ms timeout and passes whatever arrives to dxl2_link_receive(). It stops after four empty reads in a row, which leaves enough time for every device to answer a broadcast PING. The handler ignores packets whose instruction is not 0x55, which removes the echo of the request on single-wire adapters. The exit code is 0 if at least one device answered.

The POSIX version supports 9600, 57600, 115200 and 230400 bit/s, and 1, 2, 3 and 4 Mbit/s where termios defines them (Linux). The Windows version accepts any rate the adapter supports.

docs.title: Zephyr
docs.text:
examples/zephyr is a Zephyr application that makes a board a DYNAMIXEL device answering PING. It is the structure used in production firmware, reduced to the library API.

  • The UART interrupt reads the FIFO and puts each byte into a k_msgq. It never calls the library.
  • An RX thread, created with K_THREAD_DEFINE, owns the link: it waits on the queue and passes each byte to dxl2_link_receive(). The packet handler runs in this thread.
  • The write function sends with uart_poll_out() under a mutex, so other threads may send on the same link.

Select the UART with a dxl2,uart chosen node in a board overlay (a template is in app.overlay.example) and build with west:

west build -b <board> examples/zephyr -- -DDTC_OVERLAY_FILE=<board>.overlay

The application's CMakeLists.txt includes dxl2.cmake and links the dxl2 target to zephyr_interface, so the library is compiled with the board's architecture flags. The console must not use the same UART: text output corrupts the packet framing.

docs.title: Extending the Library
docs.text: DXL2-C is intentionally small: it implements the wire format and stops there. This chapter shows where the extension points are, how to build the common higher-level pieces on top of the public API, and how to change the library itself when that is the right thing to do.

docs.title: Where to extend
docs.text:
You want to… Do it in Library change needed? Support another transport (RS-485, USB CDC, TCP, CAN gateway) your write function and receive loop No Emulate a device model your packet handler and Control Table No Send SYNC, BULK or other multi-device instructions parameter builders on top of dxl2_link_send() No Use a private, vendor-specific instruction your handler; the codec passes any instruction byte through No Handle bigger packets DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE No, configuration only Run several buses one struct dxl2_link per bus No Fix a bug or change wire-format behavior the library sources Yes — see Contributing

Almost everything is done on top of the library. Keep it that way: your extensions stay portable, and you can update DXL2-C without merging changes.

docs.title: Adding a transport
docs.text:
A transport needs two pieces of code.

Receive. Deliver received bytes to dxl2_link_receive() from one context. Any chunking works. Typical shapes:

Transport Receive loop UART with RX interrupt ISR writes to a ring buffer; main loop or thread drains it UART with DMA Idle-line or half/full-transfer interrupt signals a thread; the thread passes the new region USB CDC / TCP socket Pass each received block as it arrives Log file or capture Read the file in blocks and pass them in order

Transmit. Implement dxl2_write_fn:

typedef int (*dxl2_write_fn)(void* context, const uint8_t* data, size_t length);

The contract:

  • data is one complete packet, header to CRC. Send all length bytes in order, without interleaving other output.
  • Return 0 on success or a negative value on failure; the value is returned by dxl2_link_send*(). Avoid -1, which is DXL2_PARSE_ERROR.
  • The buffer is valid only during the call. A buffered or DMA transmitter must copy it.
  • On a half-duplex bus, enable the driver before the first byte and switch back to receive when the last byte has left the shift register — not when the FIFO is empty.
  • If several contexts can send, serialize the calls with a mutex.

Use write_context to pass your driver instance, so one write function serves several buses:

struct uart_port; /* your driver */
int uart_port_write(struct uart_port* port, const uint8_t* data, size_t length);

static int link_write(void* context, const uint8_t* data, size_t length)
{
    return uart_port_write((struct uart_port*) context, data, length);
}

static struct dxl2_link bus_a;
static struct dxl2_link bus_b;

void buses_init(struct uart_port* port_a, struct uart_port* port_b)
{
    const struct dxl2_link_config config_a = {.write = link_write, .write_context = port_a};
    const struct dxl2_link_config config_b = {.write = link_write, .write_context = port_b};

    (void) dxl2_link_init(&bus_a, &config_a);
    (void) dxl2_link_init(&bus_b, &config_b);
}

docs.title: Building a Control Table
docs.text:
A device is mostly a register map. A table-driven description keeps the READ and WRITE handlers generic and makes range and access checks automatic:

enum access
{
    ACCESS_R,  /* read-only */
    ACCESS_RW, /* read-write, RAM */
    ACCESS_RW_EEPROM, /* read-write only while torque is off */
};

struct item
{
    uint16_t address;
    uint8_t size;
    enum access access;
};

static const struct item items[] = {
    {0U, 2U, ACCESS_R},           /* Model Number */
    {6U, 1U, ACCESS_R},           /* Firmware Version */
    {7U, 1U, ACCESS_RW_EEPROM},   /* ID */
    {64U, 1U, ACCESS_RW},         /* Torque Enable */
    {65U, 1U, ACCESS_RW},         /* LED */
    {116U, 4U, ACCESS_RW},        /* Goal Position */
    {132U, 4U, ACCESS_R},         /* Present Position */
};

static uint8_t table[CONTROL_TABLE_SIZE];

/* DXL2_ERR_NONE if [address, address + length) may be written now. */
static uint8_t check_write(uint16_t address, uint16_t length, bool torque_on)
{
    uint8_t error = DXL2_ERR_NONE;

    for (size_t i = 0U; i < (sizeof(items) / sizeof(items[0])); ++i)
    {
        const struct item* item = &items[i];
        const bool overlaps = (item->address < (address + length))
                              && (address < (item->address + item->size));

        if (overlaps && ((item->access == ACCESS_R)
                         || ((item->access == ACCESS_RW_EEPROM) && torque_on)))
        {
            error = DXL2_ERR_ACCESS;
        }
    }
    return error;
}

Apply side effects after the write — for example, a new ID takes effect after the Status Packet has been sent with the old one. The simulator of DXL2 Studio (tools/dxl2_gui/native/dxl2_sim.c) is a complete reference implementation of an X-series Control Table, including REG_WRITE/ACTION, FACTORY_RESET, SYNC and BULK instructions.

docs.title: Building instruction parameters
docs.text:
The codec encodes any instruction; it does not need to know its parameter layout. Build the parameters with the little-endian helpers and send them with dxl2_link_send().

Instruction Parameters READ address (2), length (2) WRITE, REG_WRITE address (2), data (n) SYNC_READ, FAST_SYNC_READ address (2), length (2), ID (1) × devices SYNC_WRITE address (2), length (2), then per device: ID (1), data (length) BULK_READ, FAST_BULK_READ per device: ID (1), address (2), length (2) BULK_WRITE per device: ID (1), address (2), length (2), data (length) FACTORY_RESET, CLEAR, BACKUP one or more option bytes, see the ROBOTIS specification

SYNC and BULK instructions are sent to the broadcast ID. A SYNC_WRITE builder that sets the 4-byte Goal Position (address 116 on X-series servos) of several servos at once:

/* Returns 0 on success, DXL2_PARSE_ERROR if the packet does not fit. */
int sync_write_u32(struct dxl2_link* link, uint16_t address, const uint8_t* ids,
                   const uint32_t* values, size_t count)
{
    uint8_t parameters[DXL2_MAX_PARAMETER_SIZE];
    size_t length = 4U;
    int result = DXL2_PARSE_ERROR;

    if ((4U + (count * 5U)) <= sizeof(parameters))
    {
        dxl2_put_u16(&parameters[0], address);
        dxl2_put_u16(&parameters[2], 4U); /* bytes per device */
        for (size_t i = 0U; i < count; ++i)
        {
            parameters[length] = ids[i];
            dxl2_put_u32(&parameters[length + 1U], values[i]);
            length += 5U;
        }
        result = dxl2_link_send(link, DXL2_BROADCAST_ID, DXL2_INST_SYNC_WRITE, parameters,
                                (uint16_t) length);
    }
    return result;
}

dxl2_link_send() also returns DXL2_PARSE_ERROR when byte stuffing makes the packet larger than DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE, so the size check above is a fast path, not the only guard.

For SYNC_READ and BULK_READ, every addressed device answers with its own Status Packet, in the order of the request; collect them in your handler as shown for broadcast PING. FAST_SYNC_READ and FAST_BULK_READ return one combined Status Packet whose parameter layout is described in the ROBOTIS specification; parse it in your handler.

docs.title: Vendor-specific instructions
docs.text: The parser and the encoder accept any instruction byte. If you control every node on a bus, you can define private instructions, for example to update firmware. Choose values that the specification does not use, keep them out of public buses, and document them — a future revision of the protocol may assign them. Do not add them to dxl2_defs.h, which only contains values from the specification.

docs.title: Bridging two buses
docs.text:
A gateway that forwards packets between two buses needs no special support: each bus gets its own link, and each handler re-sends what it receives on the other link.

static void forward_a_to_b(const struct dxl2_packet* packet, void* context)
{
    (void) context;
    (void) dxl2_link_send(&bus_b, packet->id, packet->instruction, packet->parameters,
                          packet->parameter_length);
}

Re-encoding regenerates the stuffing and the CRC, so packets that arrived corrupted are never forwarded — the parser has already dropped them.

docs.title: Changing the configuration
docs.text:
DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE is the only build-time parameter. Raise it if your devices use large READ, SYNC or BULK transfers; lower it to save RAM on small MCUs. Define it for the whole build, so that the library and the application agree on the structure sizes:

target_compile_definitions(dxl2 PUBLIC DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE=1024U)

The value must be between 10 and 65542; the build stops with an error otherwise. See Configuration for its effect on RAM and stack.

docs.title: Contributing to the library
docs.text:
Changes to DXL2-C itself are welcome when they fix a bug, follow the specification more closely, or add something every user needs. The rules keep the library certifiable:

  1. Code. C11, no new dependencies, no heap, no global mutable state. Public symbols use the dxl2_ / DXL2_ prefix and have Doxygen comments. Follow the MISRA rules used in the code: one return per function, parentheses around mixed operators, (void) for ignored results, ++/-- as separate statements, array indexing instead of pointer arithmetic.
  2. Tests. Every behavior change comes with a GoogleTest test in tests/unit/gtest_dxl2_*.cpp (register new files in dxl2.cmake). Line and branch coverage must stay at 100 %. When the codec changes, update the Python twin in tests/integration/dxl2/protocol.py; the cross-check compares both.
  3. Analysis. misra-analyze must report 0 violations. An unavoidable deviation is recorded in the deviation register.
  4. Format. clang-format with the repository .clang-format must report no changes.
  5. Documentation. Update the affected pages in docs/, the stack table in Configuration when a function's frame changes, the diagrams (python tools/docs/diagrams.py) when the structure changes, and add an entry under [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md.
  6. Compatibility. The public API is stable within a major version: do not remove or change public functions, structure members or return values without a major release.

Run the whole definition of done locally before opening a pull request:

cmake --preset "DXL2[UnitTests]" && cmake --build "build/DXL2[UnitTests]" --target coverage
cmake --preset "DXL2[IntegrationTests]" && cmake --build "build/DXL2[IntegrationTests]" --target integration_tests
cmake --preset "DXL2[Debug]" && cmake --build "build/DXL2[Debug]" --target misra-analyze
cmake --preset "DXL2[Examples]" && cmake --build "build/DXL2[Examples]" && ctest --test-dir "build/DXL2[Examples]" -L example

Pull requests target the development branch. CI runs the same checks and blocks the merge if any of them fails.

docs.title: DXL2 Studio
docs.text: DXL2 Studio is a desktop application for testing and debugging DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 communication. It is built on the DXL2-C static library itself: every Instruction Packet it sends is encoded by dxl2_link_send() and every byte it receives goes through dxl2_link_receive(). What you see in the tool is exactly what the library does.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
Mode What runs on each side Hardware Simulation The controller and a simulated DYNAMIXEL device (XL430-W250 Control Table) each run the library on their own link None Serial port The controller runs on the library and talks to a real device over a COM port: a board with DXL2-C, a U2D2 adapter, or a servo USB-to-serial adapter

The simulation makes it possible to learn the protocol, try instructions and test error handling without any hardware. The serial mode turns the same tool into a bus analyzer for your own firmware.

docs.title: Installation and start
docs.text:
DXL2 Studio needs Python 3.8 or newer with Tkinter, CMake 3.20 or newer and a C11 compiler (GCC/MinGW-w64, Clang or MSVC, with the same bitness as Python).

python -m pip install -r tools/dxl2_gui/requirements.txt   # pyserial, for the serial mode
python tools/dxl2_gui/dxl2_gui.py

On the first start the tool offers to build its native bridge, a shared library that links the static libdxl2.a. You can also build it by hand:

cmake -S tools/dxl2_gui/native -B tools/dxl2_gui/build
cmake --build tools/dxl2_gui/build --config Release

Command-line options select the mode and connect at once:

python tools/dxl2_gui/dxl2_gui.py --mode sim --id 1 --connect
python tools/dxl2_gui/dxl2_gui.py --mode serial --port COM3 --baud 1000000 --connect

In VS Code, open the task menu (Ctrl+Shift+B), run Python: Setup venv once, then GUI: Run (Simulation) or GUI: Run (Serial port).

On Debian and Ubuntu, install the system packages first and add your user to the dialout group to use USB serial adapters without root:

sudo apt install python3-venv python3-tk cmake build-essential
sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER   # log out and back in afterwards

docs.title: Window layout
docs.text:
The window has three areas:

  • Connection bar (top): mode, simulated device ID or serial port and baud rate, reply timeout, and the Connect button (F5).
  • Control tabs (left): quick control, packet builder, Control Table, bus scan and simulator settings.
  • Communication debugger (right): the packet log, the field-by-field breakdown of the selected packet and its raw bytes. The status bar below shows packet and byte counters, invalid packets, timeouts, status errors and latency.

docs.title: Quick control
docs.text: Ping, reboot, factory reset, torque and LED on and off, and the Hardware Error Status. A slider sends the Goal Position; Auto-poll reads the Present Position every 200 ms.

docs.title: Control Table
docs.text: Read all reads every item with one READ instruction. Items whose value changed since the last read are highlighted, and Auto refresh repeats the read every 500 ms. Double-click a read-write item to write a new value. The view uses the X-series layout; for other models use the packet builder.

docs.title: Packet builder
docs.text:
Choose an instruction and fill in its fields — or type raw parameters in hex for SYNC and BULK instructions — and the preview shows the exact packet that dxl2_encode() produces, including byte stuffing and CRC.

The Raw bytes sender bypasses the encoder. Its Break CRC, Truncate and Add noise buttons create invalid input, so you can watch how a receiver — the simulated device or your own firmware — rejects it and recovers.

docs.title: Bus scan
docs.text: Ping every ID in a range, or send one broadcast PING. The results list the model number, firmware version and latency of every device. Double-click a result to make it the target of the other tabs.

docs.title: Simulator
docs.text:
In simulation mode this tab injects faults into the replies of the simulated device: drop a percentage of replies, corrupt one bit, add a delay, or split a reply into two chunks. You can also set a Hardware Error Status (which sets the alert bit in every Status Packet), watch the device state and power-cycle the device.

The simulated device implements PING, READ, WRITE, REG_WRITE/ACTION, FACTORY_RESET, REBOOT, CLEAR, BACKUP, SYNC_READ/WRITE and BULK_READ/WRITE, applies Status Return Level, the EEPROM lock while torque is on, and the ID, torque and LED range checks. It answers FAST_SYNC_READ and FAST_BULK_READ with an Instruction Error.

docs.title: Communication debugger
docs.text:
Every log entry has a time stamp, the time since the previous entry and, for replies, the round-trip time (rt). Entries are color coded:

Entry Meaning TX Instruction Packet sent RX Status Packet received; interpreted against its request (for example Present Position=2048) TIMEOUT No reply within the reply timeout ERR Bytes rejected by dxl2_link_receive() — on the controller or on the simulated device INFO Connection and tool messages

Select an entry to see it field by field — header, ID, Length check, instruction, error, parameters (with a note when byte stuffing is present) and CRC check. Raw RX chunks shows the bytes exactly as the transport delivered them, before decoding. The log can be filtered, paused, cleared and exported to CSV or text (Ctrl+E).

For serial ports, Discard echo removes your own bytes from the receive stream on single-wire half-duplex buses, and the port field accepts pyserial URLs such as socket://192.168.1.10:5000 for serial-over-TCP bridges.

docs.title: How the tool uses the library
docs.text:
tools/dxl2_gui/
├── dxl2_gui.py          entry point
├── dxl2gui/
│   ├── app.py           Tkinter user interface
│   ├── session.py       request queue, timeouts, statistics, log entries
│   ├── transport.py     simulation and serial transports, fault injection
│   ├── native.py        ctypes binding and CMake build helper
│   └── decode.py        names, packet breakdown, value formatting
└── native/
    ├── dxl2_host.c/.h   controller side: dxl2_link_send / dxl2_link_receive
    ├── dxl2_sim.c/.h    simulated device on its own dxl2_link
    └── CMakeLists.txt   links the static dxl2 target into dxl2_gui_native

The native bridge exports only dxl2_host_* and dxl2_sim_* functions. Python never depends on the memory layout of the library structures: it asks the bridge for their sizes and treats them as opaque. dxl2_sim.c is also a useful reference if you write your own device firmware: it is a complete X-series Control Table on top of the public API.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This chapter shows how to get DXL2-C, add it to your project, and build and test it.

docs.title: Get the library
docs.text:
Clone the repository, or download a release package from the GitHub releases page:

git clone https://github.com/AntonVynohradov/DXL2-C.git

Each release provides the source code, a prebuilt static library for Linux x86-64 with its headers, and the MISRA report.

docs.title: Add it to your project
docs.text:
The library is two C files and five headers. Choose whichever fits your build:

CMake. Include dxl2.cmake; it defines the static library target dxl2 with its include directories and version definitions:

include(path/to/DXL2-C/dxl2.cmake)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE dxl2)

Any other build system (Make, IDE projects, vendor tools). Compile src/dxl2_protocol.c and src/dxl2_link.c with your firmware and add the repository root and inc/ to the include path. No other files and no special flags are needed.

Prebuilt package. Link lib/libdxl2.a and add include/ to the include path. Use it only for the platform it was built for.

Then include the umbrella header and continue with Using the Library:

#include "dxl2.h"

docs.title: Prerequisites for development
docs.text:
• C11 compiler (GCC, Clang, or an embedded toolchain)
  • CMake 3.20+
  • Optional: GoogleTest and gcovr (unit tests, coverage), Python 3 and pytest (integration tests), Cppcheck (static analysis, MISRA C:2012 addon), clang-format, MkDocs with mkdoxy (documentation)

docs.title: Build with presets
docs.text:
Preset Purpose DXL2[Debug] Static library, -g, DXL2_DEBUG defined DXL2[Release] Static library, -O2 -DNDEBUG DXL2[UnitTests] GoogleTest executable with coverage instrumentation DXL2[IntegrationTests] pytest suite run through CTest DXL2[Examples] Host examples and the bare-metal simulation test 
cmake --preset "DXL2[Debug]"
cmake --build "build/DXL2[Debug]"

All builds use -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion.

docs.title: Unit tests and coverage
docs.text:
cmake --preset "DXL2[UnitTests]"
cmake --build "build/DXL2[UnitTests]" --target coverage

The coverage target builds the tests, runs them through CTest and writes an HTML report to build/DXL2[UnitTests]/Coverage/coverage.html. It fails when line or branch coverage of src/ is below DXL2_COVERAGE_MIN (100 %).

docs.title: Integration tests
docs.text:
python -m pip install pytest
cmake --preset "DXL2[IntegrationTests]"
cmake --build "build/DXL2[IntegrationTests]" --target integration_tests

The suite in tests/integration/ tests the Python codec and compiles src/dxl2_protocol.c with gcc to compare 300 random packets between the C and Python implementations. The cross-check is skipped when gcc is not on the path.

docs.title: Static analysis
docs.text:
From any configured build directory:

Target Tool cppcheck-analyze Cppcheck, all checks, report in cppcheck.txt misra-analyze Cppcheck MISRA C:2012 addon on src/, report in misra.txt codeql-analyze CodeQL cpp-queries, report in codeql-report.sarif

misra-analyze fails when the report contains a violation; see MISRA C:2012 for the deviation register.

MISRA rule texts are not distributed with Cppcheck. If you have a licensed copy, pass it with -DDXL2_MISRA_RULE_TEXTS=<file> to get rule headlines in the report.

docs.title: Formatting
docs.text:
clang-format -i src/*.c inc/*.h dxl2.h tests/unit/*.cpp tests/unit/*.h examples/*/*.[ch] examples/zephyr/src/*.c

CI rejects pull requests with unformatted C/C++ files.

docs.title: Versioning and releases
docs.text:
cmake/version.cmake takes the version from the latest vX.Y.Z Git tag and passes it as DXL2_VERSION_MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH and the string DXL2_VERSION. Without a tag it uses DXL2_DEFAULT_VERSION and prints a warning; keep the fallback values in dxl2.h equal to that default (a unit test checks that the string matches the numbers).

To release version X.Y.Z:

  1. Set DXL2_DEFAULT_VERSION in cmake/version.cmake and the fallbacks in dxl2.h to X.Y.Z.
  2. Move the [Unreleased] entries in CHANGELOG.md to a [X.Y.Z] - date section.
  3. Merge to main, then tag and push: git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z.

The Release workflow refuses a tag that does not match these files, runs all quality gates and publishes the GitHub Release.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation is written in Markdown in docs/ and published with MkDocs (Material theme); the API pages are generated from the source comments by Doxygen through mkdoxy. Install the tools into the project virtual environment (VS Code task Python: Setup venv, or python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt) and Doxygen.

Task Command VS Code task Live preview mkdocs serve Docs: Serve on localhost Build the website into site/ mkdocs build Docs: Build site Build the printable PDF manual python tools/docs/build_manual.py Docs: Build PDF manual

The PDF manual is written to build/manual/DXL2-C_User_Manual_v<version>.pdf. It is an A4 document with a cover page, an imprint, a table of contents with page numbers, numbered chapters, running headers, page numbers and PDF bookmarks. It needs WeasyPrint, which uses the Pango library: on Linux install libpango-1.0-0 and libpangoft2-1.0-0 (Debian, Ubuntu); on Windows install the MSYS2 package mingw-w64-x86_64-pango — the script finds C:\msys64\mingw64\bin by itself, or set WEASYPRINT_DLL_DIRECTORIES.

Diagrams are SVG files generated by python tools/docs/diagrams.py; edit the script, not the SVG files.

docs.title: Integration Guide
docs.text:
The library does not touch hardware. An integration has three parts:

  1. Receive: move bytes from the transport into dxl2_link_receive(). Do it in a thread or the main loop, not in an interrupt handler: the packet handler runs in the caller's context and usually sends a reply.
  2. Transmit: a dxl2_write_fn that writes a complete packet. Serialize it (mutex) if more than one thread can send.
  3. Application: a dxl2_packet_handler_t that interprets the instruction for its IDs (Control Table) and answers with dxl2_link_send_status().

Complete, buildable programs for each pattern below are described in Examples.

docs.title: Zephyr: UART with an RX interrupt, byte queue and RX thread
docs.text:
examples/zephyr is the structure used in the SmartManipulator-X firmware, reduced to the library API. The ISR only queues bytes; a thread owns the link. Select the UART with a dxl2,uart chosen node (see app.overlay.example) and build it with:

west build -b <board> examples/zephyr -- -DDTC_OVERLAY_FILE=<board>.overlay

Notes from the hardware bring-up:

  • Size the byte queue for at least one maximum packet plus the time the handler blocks (for example while it waits for a motor driver). A dropped byte makes the next packet fail its CRC; the parser recovers on the next header.
  • uart_poll_out() is simple and deterministic. At 230400 bit/s a 256-byte packet takes about 11 ms; use interrupt or DMA TX if that is too long.
  • Check the real bit rate of the UART divisor. A 16550-style UART at a 50 MHz clock gives 223214 bit/s for 230400 (-3.1 %), which is too far off; some UARTs (for example the SmartFusion2 MMUART) have a fractional divisor.
  • Text output (console, logs, printk) on the same UART corrupts the framing.

docs.title: Adding the library to a CMake build (Zephyr or any other)
docs.text:
dxl2.cmake defines the dxl2 static library target with its include directories (. and inc/) and the version definitions:

include(path/to/dxl2/dxl2.cmake)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE dxl2)

In a Zephyr application also link the library to zephyr_interface, so it is compiled with the board's architecture flags (see examples/zephyr/CMakeLists.txt):

target_link_libraries(dxl2 PUBLIC zephyr_interface)

Without CMake, compile src/*.c and add the repository root and inc/ to the include path. Buffer sizes are set in inc/dxl2_config.h and can be overridden with compiler definitions (for example -DDXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE=1024U).

docs.title: Bare metal / other RTOS
docs.text: The same pattern applies (examples/bare_metal): ring buffer from the RX interrupt, drain it from the main loop into dxl2_link_receive(), and a blocking or buffered write function. On a host (Linux/Windows serial port, examples/host_serial) read whatever the port returns and pass it to dxl2_link_receive() in one call.

docs.title: Answering a device request
docs.text:
A device implementation typically does this in the handler:

static void on_packet(const struct dxl2_packet *packet, void *context)
{
    const uint8_t *p = packet->parameters;

    if (packet->id != MY_ID && packet->id != DXL2_BROADCAST_ID) {
        return;
    }
    switch (packet->instruction) {
    case DXL2_INST_PING:
        /* model number (2), firmware version (1) */
        break;
    case DXL2_INST_READ:
        if (packet->parameter_length != 4U) {
            dxl2_link_send_status(&link, MY_ID, DXL2_ERR_DATA_LENGTH, NULL, 0U);
            return;
        }
        /* address = dxl2_get_u16(&p[0]), length = dxl2_get_u16(&p[2]) */
        break;
    default:
        dxl2_link_send_status(&link, MY_ID, DXL2_ERR_INSTRUCTION, NULL, 0U);
        break;
    }
}

Do not answer instructions sent to the broadcast ID, except PING (all devices answer, ordered by ID) and the read instructions that name the device in their ID list. Respect the device's Status Return Level and Return Delay Time registers if it emulates them.

docs.title: MISRA C:2012 compliance
docs.text: This page records how the library is checked against MISRA C:2012 and every deviation from it. It covers the library code only: src/, inc/ and dxl2.h. Tests, examples and tools are not in scope.

docs.title: Checking
docs.text:
Check Where Gate Cppcheck MISRA C:2012 addon misra-analyze target, CI job MISRA C:2012 Analysis Fails on any violation Cppcheck, all checks cppcheck-analyze target, CI job Cppcheck Analysis Report CodeQL cpp-queries codeql-analyze target, CI job CodeQL Analysis Report Compiler -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion No warnings Manual review Pull request review, see .github/.copilot-instructions.md Reviewer

misra-analyze fails when the report contains a violation. Set -DDXL2_MISRA_FAIL_ON_VIOLATION=OFF to get the report without failing the build. A violation that cannot be fixed must be added to the deviation register below before the pull request is merged.

The Cppcheck addon checks most decidable rules, but not the directives or rules that need knowledge of the whole program or the intent of the code. Those are covered by the manual review notes below.

docs.title: Current status
docs.text: Item Result Cppcheck MISRA addon (2.13 in CI, 2.16) 0 violations Unit test coverage of src/ 100 % lines, 100 % branches Deviations 3, all advisory, listed below

docs.title: Manual review notes
docs.text: Guideline How the library complies Dir 4.1 (run-time failures) Every array index is bounded by a length check or by the DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE invariant described in dxl2_decode_packet(). inc/dxl2_config.h rejects a DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE outside 10..65542 at compile time. Dir 4.11 (validity of arguments) Every public function checks its pointer arguments and lengths and returns DXL2_PARSE_ERROR (or 0 for dxl2_crc16() and the counters). The inline little-endian helpers in dxl2_defs.h do not check: they take a pointer to 2 or 4 readable bytes, like memcpy(). Dir 4.12, Rule 21.3 (dynamic memory) No heap. All state is in caller-owned structures. Rule 15.5 (single point of exit) Every function has one return at the end. Rule 17.2 (recursion) No recursion; the stack depth is fixed, see Configuration. Rule 21.6 (standard I/O) No <stdio.h>. The library includes only <stddef.h>, <stdint.h>, <stdbool.h> and <string.h>.

docs.title: DEV-01: int as the status type (Dir 4.6, advisory)
docs.text:
• Location: return type of dxl2_parser_feed(), dxl2_encode(), dxl2_link_init(), dxl2_link_send(), dxl2_link_send_status() and of the dxl2_write_fn callback.
  • Rationale: the value is a status code (-1, 0, 1, or the code the write callback returned), not a quantity whose size matters. int lets an integrator pass an existing driver write() function as dxl2_write_fn without a wrapper. int is at least 16 bits on every conforming compiler, which holds every value the library returns.
  • Risk control: the library never does arithmetic on these values; it only compares them with 0 or DXL2_PARSE_ERROR.

docs.title: DEV-02: macros not used inside the library (Rule 2.5, advisory)
docs.text:
• Location: DXL2_INST_* (except DXL2_INST_STATUS), DXL2_ERR_*, DXL2_MAX_ID, DXL2_BROADCAST_ID in inc/dxl2_defs.h; DXL2_VERSION_* in dxl2.h.
  • Rationale: these are the public names of the protocol constants. They are used by applications, not by the codec, which handles every instruction the same way.

docs.title: DEV-03: external functions referenced in one translation unit (Rule 8.7, advisory)
docs.text:
• Location: the public API functions that the library itself does not call, for example dxl2_link_rx_packets() and dxl2_link_invalid_packets().
  • Rationale: they are the library interface and are called by applications. Giving them internal linkage would remove them from the API.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: DXL2-C is a C11 library that implements the wire format of the ROBOTIS DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0: how packets are framed, protected with a CRC, byte-stuffed and parsed from a stream of bytes. It is written for embedded systems that must be predictable and reviewable, and it runs unchanged on microcontrollers, under an RTOS and on a PC.

docs.title: What the library does
docs.text:
• Encodes packets. Given an ID, an instruction and parameters, it builds the complete wire packet: header, Length field, byte stuffing and CRC-16.
  • Parses a byte stream. It accepts bytes in any chunking, finds packet headers, validates Length and CRC, removes byte stuffing and hands you complete packets. It resynchronizes by itself after noise or lost bytes.
  • Connects the codec to a transport. The link layer owns a parser, calls your handler for every valid packet and sends replies through a write function you supply.
  • Defines the protocol constants. Every instruction and status error value of the specification, plus helpers for little-endian fields.

docs.title: What the library does not do
docs.text:
DXL2-C is deliberately limited to the wire format. These belong to your application:

Concern Why it is not in the library UART, RS-485, USB or socket drivers They are hardware- and OS-specific. You pass bytes in and provide a write function. Threads, queues, interrupts, locking Every system has its own. The integration guide shows the usual patterns. Control Tables and device models Addresses and registers differ between models. Your handler interprets READ, WRITE and the other instructions. Timeouts and retries A controller decides how long to wait for a reply; the library has no clock. Higher-level helpers (SYNC_WRITE builders, servo APIs) They are easy to build on top of the codec; see Extending the Library.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text:
• Device firmware. A board that should behave like a DYNAMIXEL device — a custom actuator, a sensor hub or a gripper — on an existing DYNAMIXEL bus.
  • Controller firmware. A microcontroller that drives DYNAMIXEL servos directly.
  • Host tools. Test benches, production tools and debuggers that need a codec which behaves exactly like the firmware. DXL2 Studio is such a tool.

docs.title: Key properties
docs.text: Property Value Language C11 (-std=c11), compiles without warnings with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion Dependencies <stddef.h>, <stdint.h>, <stdbool.h>, <string.h> only Memory No heap; all state in caller-owned structures; sizes fixed by DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE RAM per link about 2 × DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE + 40 bytes (≈ 550 bytes with the default 256) Stack at most about 600 bytes on Cortex-M4 for the transmit path (details) Coding standard MISRA C:2012, 0 Cppcheck addon violations, 3 advisory deviations Tests 100 % line and branch coverage; C/Python cross-check; ROBOTIS reference packets Thread safety None built in, by design; see Threading and reentrancy License Apache License 2.0

docs.title: Terminology
docs.text: Controller The node that sends Instruction Packets and waits for replies. ROBOTIS documentation also calls it the main controller or master. Device A node with an ID (0–252) that executes instructions and answers with Status Packets: a servo, a sensor, or your firmware built with DXL2-C. Instruction Packet A packet sent by the controller. Its instruction byte says what to do (PING, READ, WRITE, …). Status Packet The reply of a device. Its instruction byte is 0x55 and its first parameter is the error byte. Broadcast ID ID 254 (0xFE). Every device executes the instruction; only some instructions are answered. Control Table The register map of a device. Not part of the protocol itself and not part of this library. Byte stuffing The rule that keeps the header sequence out of the packet body. See Byte stuffing.

docs.title: Conventions in this documentation
docs.text:
• Hexadecimal bytes are written without a prefix inside packets (FF FF FD 00) and with 0x in text and code (0x55).
  • Multi-byte fields are little endian, as on the wire.
  • DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE is shown with its default value, 256 bytes.
  • Code examples follow the library's own style: C11, MISRA-friendly, one return per function where it matters.

docs.title: DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0
docs.text: This chapter describes the Protocol 2.0 wire format and exactly what DXL2-C does with each part of it. The normative reference is the ROBOTIS Protocol 2.0 specification.

docs.title: The bus
docs.text:
DYNAMIXEL devices share one serial line (TTL or RS-485) in a daisy chain. The line is half duplex: only one node may transmit at a time. Communication is always a request/response exchange:

  1. The controller sends an Instruction Packet addressed to one ID (0–252) or to the broadcast ID 254.
  2. The addressed device executes it and, unless the instruction was broadcast or its Status Return Level says otherwise, answers with a Status Packet after its Return Delay Time.
  3. The controller waits for the reply with a timeout before it sends the next request.

The UART format is 8 data bits, no parity, one stop bit; the bit rate is configured per device (57600 bit/s by default on most models, up to several Mbit/s).

docs.title: Packet
docs.text:
Field Offset Size Meaning Header 0 4 Always FF FF FD 00 ID 4 1 Device ID 0..252; 0xFE = broadcast (DXL2_BROADCAST_ID) Length 5 2 Little endian. Counts the instruction, the stuffed parameters and the CRC, so the minimum is 3 Instruction 7 1 DXL2_INST_*; 0x55 marks a Status Packet Parameters 8 n Instruction parameters; for a Status Packet the first byte is the error CRC 7 + Length − 2 2 Little endian, over all bytes from the header up to the CRC (stuffed)

A complete packet is therefore 7 + Length bytes long; the shortest one (no parameters) is 10 bytes. All multi-byte values inside the parameters — addresses, lengths, register values — are little endian too: use dxl2_get_u16/u32 and dxl2_put_u16/u32.

In struct dxl2_packet the library gives you the ID, the instruction and the unstuffed parameters with their count. The header, Length and CRC are consumed by the parser.

docs.title: CRC-16
docs.text: Polynomial 0x8005, initial value 0, not reflected, no final XOR (the CRC-16/BUYPASS variant). It is computed over the stuffed packet. The ROBOTIS PING reference packet FF FF FD 00 01 03 00 01 has CRC 0x4E19 (transmitted as 19 4E). The CRC is computed bit by bit without a lookup table, which keeps the code small; its execution time depends only on the length.

docs.title: Byte stuffing
docs.text:
So that a header never appears inside a packet, the sender inserts an extra 0xFD after every FF FF FD sequence in the instruction/parameter area, and the receiver removes it. The Length field counts the stuffed bytes.

The rule applies to the whole area after the Length field — instruction and parameters — so a sequence that starts in the instruction byte is stuffed too.

dxl2_encode() stuffs while it writes. The parser checks the CRC over the stuffed bytes first, then unstuffs. An FF FF FD that is not followed by FD is a malformed packet (DXL2_PARSE_ERROR).

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
Value Name Value Name 0x01 PING 0x55 STATUS (reply) 0x02 READ 0x82 SYNC_READ 0x03 WRITE 0x83 SYNC_WRITE 0x04 REG_WRITE 0x8A FAST_SYNC_READ 0x05 ACTION 0x92 BULK_READ 0x06 FACTORY_RESET 0x93 BULK_WRITE 0x08 REBOOT 0x9A FAST_BULK_READ 0x10 CLEAR 0x20 BACKUP

Parameter layouts of the common instructions:

Instruction Parameters PING none; reply data: model number (2), firmware version (1) READ address (2), length (2); reply data: length bytes WRITE / REG_WRITE address (2), data (n) SYNC_READ address (2), length (2), ID list SYNC_WRITE address (2), length (2), then per device: ID (1) + data (length)

The library encodes and decodes every instruction the same way; interpreting the parameters (the Control Table) is up to the application.

docs.title: Status Packet error byte
docs.text: Value DXL2_ERR_* Meaning 0x00 NONE OK 0x01 RESULT_FAIL Instruction could not be processed 0x02 INSTRUCTION Undefined instruction, or ACTION without REG_WRITE 0x03 CRC CRC mismatch 0x04 DATA_RANGE Value outside the register range 0x05 DATA_LENGTH Data shorter than the register 0x06 DATA_LIMIT Value outside the configured limit 0x07 ACCESS Read-only / write-only / torque-locked register bit 7 ALERT_BIT Device has a hardware error (Hardware Error Status)

docs.title: Parser behavior
docs.text:
dxl2_parser_feed() takes one byte at a time:

  1. Bytes before a complete FF FF FD 00 header are discarded (sliding window), so the parser resynchronizes after noise or a lost byte.
  2. After 7 bytes it reads Length. A Length below 3 or one that would exceed DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE (256 bytes on the wire by default, see inc/dxl2_config.h) is rejected at once.
  3. When the whole packet is in, it checks the CRC, then unstuffs into struct dxl2_packet and returns 1.
  4. Any error returns DXL2_PARSE_ERROR and resets the parser; keep feeding bytes, the next packet is found normally.

The bytes of a rejected packet are discarded, including any that follow its header. If a byte was lost so that the Length field counts into the next packet, that packet is rejected too and the parser resynchronizes on the one after it. A controller should therefore treat a missing reply as a timeout and retry, as the ROBOTIS DynamixelSDK does.

The output packet is not touched while a packet is incomplete or when its CRC is wrong. After any error its contents are undefined: use it only when dxl2_parser_feed() returns 1.

docs.title: Using the Library
docs.text: This chapter shows how to use DXL2-C in the three typical roles: as a device that answers instructions, as a controller that drives devices, and as a plain codec without the link layer. All examples use only the public API from dxl2.h.

docs.title: Setting up a link
docs.text:
Every link needs two things from you: a function that writes bytes to the transport and a function that handles received packets.

#include "dxl2.h"

static struct dxl2_link bus;

/* Write one complete packet. Return 0 on success, a negative value on failure. */
static int bus_write(void* context, const uint8_t* data, size_t length)
{
    (void) context;
    return uart_write_blocking(data, length);
}

/* Called for every valid packet received on the bus. */
static void bus_handler(const struct dxl2_packet* packet, void* context)
{
    (void) context;
    /* see below */
}

void bus_init(void)
{
    const struct dxl2_link_config config = {
        .write = bus_write,
        .write_context = NULL,
        .handler = bus_handler,
        .handler_context = NULL,
    };

    (void) dxl2_link_init(&bus, &config);
}
  • dxl2_link_init() copies the configuration, so config can be a local variable.
  • The two context pointers are passed back unchanged to your callbacks. Use them to reach your driver or application object without global variables.
  • A link without a write function is receive-only: sending returns DXL2_PARSE_ERROR. A link without a handler still parses and counts packets.

Then move received bytes into the link wherever your transport delivers them:

void bus_poll(void)
{
    uint8_t bytes[64];
    const size_t count = uart_read_nonblocking(bytes, sizeof(bytes));

    dxl2_link_receive(&bus, bytes, count);
}

Chunk boundaries do not matter: one byte at a time, whole packets or several packets at once all give the same result.

docs.title: Writing a device
docs.text:
A device answers Instruction Packets addressed to its ID. The handler receives each decoded packet; packet->parameters holds the unstuffed parameters and packet->parameter_length their number.

#define MY_ID 1U

static uint8_t control_table[128];

static void bus_handler(const struct dxl2_packet* packet, void* context)
{
    const bool broadcast = (packet->id == DXL2_BROADCAST_ID);

    (void) context;
    if ((packet->id != MY_ID) && !broadcast)
    {
        return; /* addressed to another device */
    }

    switch (packet->instruction)
    {
        case DXL2_INST_PING:
            handle_ping();            /* every device answers a broadcast PING */
            break;
        case DXL2_INST_READ:
            if (!broadcast)
            {
                handle_read(packet);
            }
            break;
        case DXL2_INST_WRITE:
            handle_write(packet, broadcast);
            break;
        case DXL2_INST_STATUS:
            break;                    /* a reply from another device on the bus */
        default:
            if (!broadcast)
            {
                (void) dxl2_link_send_status(&bus, MY_ID, DXL2_ERR_INSTRUCTION, NULL, 0U);
            }
            break;
    }
}

docs.title: Reading parameters
docs.text:
Instruction parameters are little endian. Use the helpers from dxl2_defs.h instead of shifting bytes by hand:

/* READ: address (2 bytes), length (2 bytes) */
static void handle_read(const struct dxl2_packet* packet)
{
    if (packet->parameter_length != 4U)
    {
        (void) dxl2_link_send_status(&bus, MY_ID, DXL2_ERR_DATA_LENGTH, NULL, 0U);
    }
    else
    {
        const uint16_t address = dxl2_get_u16(&packet->parameters[0]);
        const uint16_t length = dxl2_get_u16(&packet->parameters[2]);

        if (((uint32_t) address + length) > sizeof(control_table))
        {
            (void) dxl2_link_send_status(&bus, MY_ID, DXL2_ERR_DATA_RANGE, NULL, 0U);
        }
        else
        {
            (void) dxl2_link_send_status(&bus, MY_ID, DXL2_ERR_NONE,
                                         &control_table[address], length);
        }
    }
}

Always check parameter_length before reading parameters: the library guarantees that the bytes up to parameter_length are valid, but it does not know the layout of each instruction.

docs.title: Answering
docs.text:
dxl2_link_send_status() builds the Status Packet for you: instruction 0x55, the error byte, then your data.

Error value Meaning DXL2_ERR_NONE Success DXL2_ERR_RESULT_FAIL The instruction could not be processed DXL2_ERR_INSTRUCTION Undefined instruction, or ACTION without REG_WRITE DXL2_ERR_CRC CRC mismatch (DXL2-C drops CRC-invalid packets before your handler sees them, so a device built on it normally never sends this) DXL2_ERR_DATA_RANGE Data outside the register range DXL2_ERR_DATA_LENGTH Data shorter than required DXL2_ERR_DATA_LIMIT Data outside the configured limit DXL2_ERR_ACCESS Writing a read-only register, reading a write-only one, or a locked EEPROM area

OR the error with DXL2_ERR_ALERT_BIT when your device has an active hardware error, so the controller knows to read its Hardware Error Status.

docs.title: Rules a well-behaved device follows
docs.text:
These rules come from the protocol specification. The library leaves them to you because they depend on your Control Table:

  • Broadcast. Execute broadcast instructions, but do not answer them — except PING, which every device answers. On a real bus, devices answer a broadcast PING in ID order, each after a delay, to avoid collisions.
  • Status Return Level. If you emulate the Status Return Level register, answer only PING (level 0), only PING and READ (level 1), or everything (level 2).
  • Return Delay Time. If you emulate it, wait that long before transmitting.
  • Half duplex. Release the bus (switch the transceiver to receive) as soon as the last byte has left the UART. Your write function is the right place for that.

The bare-metal example implements PING, READ and WRITE with range and access checks on a small Control Table.

docs.title: Writing a controller
docs.text:
A controller sends Instruction Packets and receives Status Packets through the same link. Because the library has no clock, your application sends the request, then keeps feeding received bytes until the reply arrives or its own timeout expires.

struct pending_reply
{
    uint8_t id;          /* the device we expect an answer from */
    bool received;
    uint8_t error;
    uint8_t data[8];
    uint16_t data_length;
};

static void controller_handler(const struct dxl2_packet* packet, void* context)
{
    struct pending_reply* reply = context;

    /* Ignore our own Instruction Packets echoed by a single-wire adapter. */
    if ((packet->instruction == DXL2_INST_STATUS) && (packet->id == reply->id)
        && (packet->parameter_length >= 1U)
        && ((packet->parameter_length - 1U) <= sizeof(reply->data)))
    {
        reply->error = packet->parameters[0];
        reply->data_length = (uint16_t) (packet->parameter_length - 1U);
        (void) memcpy(reply->data, &packet->parameters[1], reply->data_length);
        reply->received = true;
    }
}

/* Read the 4-byte Present Position (address 132 on X-series servos). */
static int read_present_position(uint8_t id, int32_t* position)
{
    uint8_t parameters[4];
    int result = -1;

    pending.id = id;
    pending.received = false;
    dxl2_put_u16(&parameters[0], 132U); /* address */
    dxl2_put_u16(&parameters[2], 4U);   /* length */

    if (dxl2_link_send(&bus, id, DXL2_INST_READ, parameters, sizeof(parameters)) == 0)
    {
        const uint32_t start = millis();

        while (!pending.received && ((millis() - start) < 20U))
        {
            bus_poll(); /* feeds dxl2_link_receive() */
        }
        if (pending.received && (pending.error == DXL2_ERR_NONE) && (pending.data_length == 4U))
        {
            *position = (int32_t) dxl2_get_u32(pending.data);
            result = 0;
        }
    }
    return result;
}

Here pending is a struct pending_reply passed as handler_context when the link is initialized, and millis() is your system tick.

Points to keep in mind:

  • Echo. On a single-wire half-duplex bus without echo cancellation, your own Instruction Packet comes back to you. It is a valid packet with your instruction byte, so filter on DXL2_INST_STATUS.
  • Timeouts. Choose a timeout that covers the device's Return Delay Time plus the transmission time of the reply. Retry on timeout: a corrupted reply is dropped silently by the parser.
  • Broadcast PING. Several devices answer one after another. Keep feeding bytes for a while and collect every Status Packet; the host serial example does exactly that.
  • SYNC and BULK instructions. Build their parameter blocks with dxl2_put_u16() and dxl2_put_u32() and send them with dxl2_link_send(); see Extending the Library.

docs.title: Using the codec without a link
docs.text:
The codec functions work on plain buffers. This is useful in tools, tests, gateways, or firmware that already has its own message loop.

Encoding a packet into your own buffer:

uint8_t packet[DXL2_MAX_PACKET_SIZE];
size_t packet_length = 0U;

if (dxl2_encode(1U, DXL2_INST_PING, NULL, 0U, packet, sizeof(packet), &packet_length) == 0)
{
    /* packet[0 .. packet_length - 1] = FF FF FD 00 01 03 00 01 19 4E */
}

Parsing a stream:

static struct dxl2_parser parser;
static struct dxl2_packet packet;

void stream_init(void)
{
    dxl2_parser_init(&parser);
}

void stream_bytes(const uint8_t* data, size_t length)
{
    for (size_t i = 0U; i < length; ++i)
    {
        const int result = dxl2_parser_feed(&parser, data[i], &packet);

        if (result == 1)
        {
            process(&packet);      /* a complete, valid packet */
        }
        else if (result < 0)
        {
            count_bad_packet();    /* keep feeding: the parser resynchronizes */
        }
        else
        {
            /* 0: need more bytes */
        }
    }
}

packet is valid only after a call that returned 1; after an error its contents are undefined. Use one parser per byte stream.

Computing a CRC directly, for example to build a test vector:

static const uint8_t ping[] = {0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFD, 0x00, 0x01, 0x03, 0x00, 0x01};
const uint16_t crc = dxl2_crc16(ping, sizeof(ping)); /* 0x4E19, sent as 19 4E */

docs.title: Return values
docs.text:
Function Success Failure dxl2_link_init() 0 DXL2_PARSE_ERROR (NULL argument) dxl2_link_send(), dxl2_link_send_status() 0 DXL2_PARSE_ERROR, or the negative value of your write function dxl2_encode() 0 DXL2_PARSE_ERROR (invalid arguments, packet does not fit) dxl2_parser_feed() 1 packet ready, 0 need more DXL2_PARSE_ERROR dxl2_crc16() the CRC 0 for a NULL buffer dxl2_link_rx_packets(), dxl2_link_invalid_packets() the counter 0 for a NULL link

DXL2_PARSE_ERROR is -1. Make your write function return other negative values for its own errors so that you can tell them apart.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
Each link counts the packets it accepted and rejected since dxl2_link_init():

const uint32_t good = dxl2_link_rx_packets(&bus);
const uint32_t bad = dxl2_link_invalid_packets(&bus);

A steadily rising invalid_packets count usually means a wrong baud rate, a baud rate error above about 2 %, a missing termination, bus contention, or text (console output, logging) on the same UART.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
The link owns a parser, dispatches every valid packet to a handler, and encodes outgoing packets into a caller-supplied write function. It has no RTOS or driver dependency: the integrator moves received bytes from the UART/USB/socket into dxl2_link_receive and provides the byte writer.

A link is not thread-safe. Call dxl2_link_receive from one context only (for example an RX thread, not an interrupt handler), and serialize dxl2_link_send calls from several contexts with a mutex.

** **

  • Lifecycle: dxl2_link_init.
  • Message flow: dxl2_link_receive, dxl2_link_send, dxl2_link_send_status.
  • Diagnostics: dxl2_link_rx_packets, dxl2_link_invalid_packets.

int dxl2_parser_feed (
    struct dxl2_parser * parser,
    uint8_t byte,
    struct dxl2_packet * packet
)

The parser searches for the Protocol 2.0 header, waits for the declared packet length, validates CRC, then removes byte stuffing. Continue feeding bytes after a parse error so the parser can find the next packet header.

Parameters:

  • parser Parser state.
  • byte Next byte from the input stream.
  • packet Output packet; its contents are valid only when the call returns 1.

Return value:

  • 1 A complete valid packet is available in packet.
  • 0 More bytes are required.
  • DXL2_PARSE_ERROR Invalid arguments or a malformed/CRC-invalid packet.
